prompt.context_jp: 派遣社員である彼女がこれから口にする一言に、正社員たち___まだ気づいてもいなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 正社員たち___まだ気づいてもいなかった。

feedback.correct_en: 正社員たち is the established group the narrator is commenting on — a topic/contrast with 彼女, so は fits. The sentence contrasts 彼女 (が) with 正社員たち (は).
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce them as new, exhaustive information, but they're the background group being commented on in contrast to 彼女.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女が話し、彼らは聞いていた。
contrast_examples.en: She spoke; they (as for them) were listening.

contrast_examples.jp: 誰が気づいた？ ― 田中さんが気づいた。

prompt.context_jp: 窓の外では鳩___電線から一斉に飛び立ち、蛍光灯の紐がわずかに揺れ始めていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 窓の外では鳩___電線から一斉に飛び立ち…

feedback.correct_en: The pigeons are newly observed — a visible event the narrator reports as it happens. New-information が fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark 鳩 as an already-established topic, but here they appear suddenly in the scene.

contrast_examples.en: Pigeons (as a topic) are symbols of peace.

prompt.context_jp: その中で春子だけ___席に残り、キーボードの上に指を置いたまま画面を見つめていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 春子だけ___席に残り…

feedback.correct_en: だけ + が signals exhaustive listing: of everyone, only Haruko stayed. This is the classic 'X alone' exhaustive-が pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: は after だけ would weaken the exclusive focus and sound unnatural in this exhaustive context.

prompt.context_jp: 春子の椅子だけ___、無人のまま静かにきしんで揺れていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 春子の椅子だけ___、無人のまま…揺れていた。

feedback.correct_en: 'Only Haruko's chair' — exhaustive-listing が picks out the one swaying chair against all others.
feedback.incorrect_en: も ('also') contradicts だけ. に marks location/direction, not the subject of 揺れていた.

contrast_examples.jp: この問題だけが解けなかった。
contrast_examples.en: Only this problem couldn't be solved.

contrast_examples.jp: この問題も解けなかった。
contrast_examples.en: This problem also couldn't be solved.

prompt.context_jp: 春子___誰よりも先に自席へ戻り、震災前と寸分違わぬ姿勢で計算表に向き直っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 春子___誰よりも先に自席へ戻り…

feedback.correct_en: Haruko is the established topic of the paragraph — the narrator describes what she, as topic, does. は fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark her as newly identified ('it was Haruko who...'), but the scene isn't answering 'who went back?' — it's narrating her habitual composure.

prompt.context_jp: 東海林の怒声___フロアを走り抜けたが、彼女の歩幅はほんの一ミリも乱れない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 東海林の怒声___フロアを走り抜けたが、彼女の歩幅は…乱れない。

feedback.correct_en: The sentence sets up a contrast: 怒声は〜/ 歩幅は〜. は on both sides highlights the parallel-but-opposite action. Contrastive は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just report an event, missing the deliberate contrast between his shouting and her unaffected stride.

contrast_examples.jp: 風は強いが、波は穏やかだ。
contrast_examples.en: The wind is strong, but the waves are calm. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 春子の靴音___遠ざかると、フロアには奇妙な静けさが降りた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 春子の靴音___遠ざかると…

feedback.correct_en: Subordinate clauses with と typically take が for the subject — it reports the event ('as her footsteps faded').
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside a 〜と time/conditional clause would sound off; は is reserved for the main topic.

contrast_examples.en: When it rains, it gets cold.

prompt.context_jp: 男たちの見せかけの権威___、たったひと言で剥がされてしまった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 男たちの見せかけの権威___、…剥がされてしまった。

feedback.correct_en: The narrator makes 'the men's facade of authority' the topic for commentary — 'as for it, it was stripped away'. Topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present it as new/identified information, but this is a summarizing comment, not a report of discovery.

prompt.context_jp: 巻き毛___本人の意志とは無関係に跳ね、その勢いだけがフロアじゅうに響き渡った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 巻き毛___本人の意志とは無関係に跳ね…

feedback.correct_en: The curly hair is newly observed in the scene — a visual event the narrator reports. New-information が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would elevate the hair to the sentence's topic, but it's a one-off vivid detail, not what the paragraph is 'about'.

contrast_examples.en: The hair (as for it) is long. (description)

prompt.context_jp: 春子___既に別の書類に目を落とし、彼の抗議を空気ほどにも扱っていない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 春子___既に別の書類に目を落とし…

feedback.correct_en: Haruko is the ongoing topic contrasted with Shōji's protest — topic/contrastive は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark her as newly identified, but she's the established figure being described.

prompt.context_jp: その角のひとつ___、後ろを通り過ぎようとした春子の後頭部を、ちょうど硬い音とともに掠めた。
prompt.prompt_jp: その角のひとつ___…春子の後頭部を…掠めた。

feedback.correct_en: The sudden incident — one corner grazing her head — is reported as a new event. が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat 'one of the corners' as a known topic, which doesn't fit this abrupt action.

contrast_examples.jp: ボールが窓に当たった。

prompt.context_jp: 東海林は…次の客をさばきに戻り、責任だけ___きれいに派遣たちの側へ流れついた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 責任だけ___きれいに派遣たちの側へ流れついた。

feedback.correct_en: だけ + が: of everything in that moment, only the blame flowed to the temps — exhaustive focus.
feedback.incorrect_en: は after だけ dilutes the sharp 'only X' punchline the narrator is making.

prompt.context_jp: 美雪さん あのね 人間の死亡率___100パーセントよ
prompt.prompt_jp: 人間の死亡率___100パーセントよ

feedback.correct_en: って is colloquial 'as for / speaking of' — Haruko states a topic she's about to comment on. Equivalent to は here.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark it as newly identified info; を doesn't fit as there's no transitive verb.

contrast_examples.en: Cats, you know, are cute. (casual topic)

prompt.context_jp: 悪いこと___派遣のせい、いいこと___自分の手柄。
prompt.prompt_jp: 悪いこと___派遣のせい、いいこと___自分の手柄。

feedback.correct_en: Classic contrastive-は pattern: X は A, Y は B. The two halves set bad vs. good things against each other.
feedback.incorrect_en: が on both sides destroys the contrast structure. Mixing は/が breaks the parallelism.

contrast_examples.en: Summers are hot; winters are cold. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 最も残業率の低い仕事___事務職の派遣だからです
prompt.prompt_jp: 最も残業率の低い仕事___事務職の派遣だからです

feedback.correct_en: 'The job WITH the lowest overtime rate IS temp office work' — 最も + が identifies/singles out one item exhaustively.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a generic topic, losing the 'it's THIS one, out of all jobs' pinpointing effect.

contrast_examples.jp: 一番速いのが新幹線だ。
contrast_examples.en: The fastest one is the shinkansen.

prompt.context_jp: 残業は 仕事のトロい 無能な社員が お給料を___するために するものです
prompt.prompt_jp: お給料を___するために
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits Haruko's biting line?

feedback.correct_en: 水増しする = 'to pad/inflate' — the sharp accusation that overtime inflates lazy workers' pay.
feedback.incorrect_en: 値引き means 'discount'; 引き算 is 'subtraction' — opposite of inflating the paycheck.

prompt.context_jp: この世に義理チョコほど ___なものは ありません
prompt.prompt_jp: この世に義理チョコほど ___なものは ありません
prompt.prompt_en: Which word captures Haruko's dismissive judgment?

feedback.correct_en: ムダ ('wasteful') matches Haruko's cold pragmatism — 'nothing in this world is more wasteful than obligation chocolate'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 大切 ('precious') or 便利 ('useful') contradict her next line telling Miyuki to save the money for retirement.

prompt.context_jp: 随分 ___ みたいだけど “派遣35歳 定年説”って 知ってる？
prompt.prompt_jp: 随分 ___ みたいだけど
prompt.prompt_en: Which expression fits the older temp's snide remark?

feedback.correct_en: 張り切る = 'to be enthusiastic/eager' — she's mocking Miyuki's rookie zeal before dropping the '35 retirement' bomb.
feedback.incorrect_en: 落ち込んでる (depressed) or 眠ってる (sleeping) wouldn't set up the sarcastic put-down that follows.

contrast_examples.jp: 新人は張り切っている。
contrast_examples.en: The newbie is all fired up.

contrast_examples.jp: 新人は落ち込んでいる。

prompt.context_jp: こんなに山積みにして ガンガン照明当てたらダメでしょ うちのチョコは ___のよ
prompt.prompt_jp: うちのチョコは ___のよ
prompt.prompt_en: What does President Hashidate claim about her chocolate?

feedback.correct_en: 'うちのチョコは生きてるのよ' ('our chocolate is alive') is her signature line — a craftsman's dramatic claim that handmade chocolate is a living thing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 冷えてる (chilled) or 甘い (sweet) are literally true but don't carry the artisan's indignation.

prompt.context_jp: 今 目の前にあることを 一生懸命やってれば いつか高い所に ___
prompt.prompt_jp: いつか高い所に ___

feedback.correct_en: 辿り着く ('to reach after effort') is the standard metaphor: hard work leads you to a higher place.
feedback.incorrect_en: 落ちる (fall) and 忘れる (forget) are the opposite of the aspirational message Satonaka wants to give.

prompt.context_jp: 会社という所は ___をつくりに行く所ですか？
prompt.prompt_jp: 会社という所は ___をつくりに行く所ですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Which word fits Haruko's cold retort?

feedback.correct_en: 仲良し ('close friends') — she's rejecting Satonaka's suggestion by framing his offer as childish friend-making.
feedback.incorrect_en: 書類 (documents) or 商品 (products) are things you do make at a company, which would make her retort meaningless.

contrast_examples.jp: 会社は仲良しクラブじゃない。
contrast_examples.en: A company isn't a friends' club.
You make products at a company.

prompt.context_jp: 俺 地震 大っ嫌いだから ___まくったよ
prompt.prompt_jp: ___まくったよ
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb matches Shōji's casual confession?

feedback.correct_en: ビビる = 'to get scared' (slang); ビビりまくる intensifies it. Matches 大っ嫌い.
feedback.incorrect_en: 笑いまくる (laughed a lot) or 寝まくる (slept a lot) contradict hating earthquakes.

prompt.context_jp: 残業というのは 社員の___の表れですよ
prompt.prompt_jp: 残業というのは 社員の___の表れですよ
prompt.prompt_en: Which noun does the boss use to justify overtime?

feedback.correct_en: 意欲 ('motivation/drive') — the boss claims overtime shows employee motivation (which Haruko then flips to 'laziness').
feedback.incorrect_en: 疲労 (fatigue) or 趣味 (hobby) wouldn't be a boss's praise of overtime.

prompt.context_jp: After the earthquake, Haruko returns to her seat and resumes work exactly as before.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for 'with the exact same posture as before the quake'?

choices.text: 震災前と寸分違わぬ姿勢で
震災前と少し違う姿勢で
震災前の姿勢をちょっと真似て

feedback.correct_en: 寸分違わぬ ('not differing by a hair') is a fixed literary expression ideal for Haruko's uncanny composure.
feedback.incorrect_en: 少し違う weakens the point; ちょっと真似て implies imitation, missing that this IS her natural posture.

contrast_examples.en: Movement identical to the smallest detail.

prompt.context_jp: Haruko rebuffs Miyuki for treating her like a counselor.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most like Haruko's crisp, formal brush-off?

choices.text: ここは 派遣の悩み相談室では ありません
ここは 派遣の悩み相談室じゃないよ
ここ 悩み聞くとこじゃないから

feedback.correct_en: The 〜ではありません form matches Haruko's clipped, formal register throughout the chapter.
feedback.incorrect_en: じゃないよ and the casual fragment don't match her businesslike persona — she almost never softens.

contrast_examples.jp: ここは図書館ではありません。
ここ図書館じゃないよ。

prompt.context_jp: Haruko refuses to take a break because the chocolate must be sold before 6pm.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing most naturally expresses 'otherwise I can't leave on time'?

choices.text: 6時までには売り切らないと 定時には帰れませんので
6時までに売り切ったら 定時には帰れませんので
6時までに売り切るので 定時に帰れますから

feedback.correct_en: 〜ないと〜ません is the standard 'if not X, then not Y' pattern — exactly Haruko's logic.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option b flips the condition (if we DO sell out, we can't leave) which is backwards. Option c is a non sequitur.

contrast_examples.jp: 急がないと間に合わない。
contrast_examples.en: If I don't hurry, I won't make it.

contrast_examples.jp: 急いだら間に合わない。
contrast_examples.en: If I hurry, I won't make it. (illogical)

prompt.context_jp: Haruko explains why she chose temp office work.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing most naturally expresses 'I want to clearly separate work hours from private time'?

choices.text: 就業時間と プライベートの時間を きっちり分けたい
就業時間と プライベートの時間を はっきり切る
仕事と プライベートの時間を かたく止めたい

feedback.correct_en: きっちり分ける is the natural collocation for cleanly dividing two things (time, roles, money).
feedback.incorrect_en: 時間を切る/止める are not standard collocations for separating work vs. private life.

contrast_examples.jp: 仕事と私生活をきっちり分ける。
contrast_examples.en: Keep work and private life strictly separate.

prompt.context_jp: Haruko's harsh assessment of defeatist temps.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line most naturally captures 'temps who say that and make no effort are already finished'?

choices.text: そう言って 何も努力しない派遣は その時点で終わってます
そう言って 何も努力しない派遣は その時点から始まります
そう言って 努力をしないの派遣は 終わるの時点です

feedback.correct_en: その時点で終わっています ('are finished at that point') is a natural, cutting idiom that matches Haruko's harsh tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option b reverses the meaning. Option c has broken grammar (努力をしないの派遣, 終わるの時点).

contrast_examples.en: The moment you give up, you've lost.
